issues.description: The Vietnamese line sounds machine-translated. 'chiếc cũ' is incomplete because it needs a noun, and 'chúng' feels unnatural when talking about one pair of jeans.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the Vietnamese to: 'Ừ, chiếc quần jeans này ấm hơn chiếc quần jeans cũ của mình.'

issues.description: The English phrase 'my old ones' may be hard for A2 listeners because 'ones' is a pronoun. I would understand 'old jeans' more quickly.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the English line to: 'Yes, they are warmer than my old jeans.'

issues.description: 'Mình mua chúng đi' is understandable, but 'chúng' sounds unnatural here and 'mình' can be a little ambiguous.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the Vietnamese to: 'Mình mua chiếc quần này đi.'

issues.description: 'Bạn' is not wrong, but if Anna and Ben are friends, 'cậu' sounds more natural in casual Vietnamese subtitles.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the Vietnamese to: 'Cậu có thích chiếc quần jeans này không?'

issues.description: The grammar note says superlatives mean 'the best in a group', but 'the cheapest' is about price, not necessarily quality. This could confuse me.
issues.suggested_fix: Rewrite the note as: Comparatives like 'warmer than' compare two things. Superlatives like 'the cheapest' say one thing has the lowest price of all.

issues.description: The hook is clear but flat. It does not make me curious about the shopping moment.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the hook to: 'Anna and Ben look for warm, cheap winter jeans.'

issues.description: The interaction prompt sounds a little stiff. A more natural question would be easier for A2 learners to answer.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the prompt to: 'Which shop near you has the cheapest clothes?'

qa_report.summary: The episode is short, simple, and mostly suitable for A2 learners. The target words and grammar point are clear, but the Vietnamese translation needs more natural phrasing, especially in line s1l2. I would listen happily after the suggested edits.
